questions.query: Retrieval that tunes its own ranking weights over time but only keeps proven improvements.
We're building an offline-first field app that must semantically search 100k manuals with zero server round-trips. What's the on-device index?
Our support bot forgets everything between sessions and customers repeat themselves; we need memory that survives restarts and can justify its recalls.
CI takes three hours. We want tests generated and prioritized only for the riskiest changed code.
Five agents work the same repo and clobber each other's context; we need coordinated roles with shared state.
Our agent ingests untrusted web content; if an ingest poisons memory we need instant rollback without replaying the whole day.
The same vector queries hit our store thousands of times an hour; we want cached reads we can cryptographically verify.
Compliance says our device mesh must stay secure even if quantum computers break RSA. What's the comms layer?
Our prompt bill doubled this quarter; we want to compress instructions without changing behavior.
The team ships code with no specs and QA finds the gaps too late; we want a phased method with hard gates from requirements to completion.
Leadership wants proof our patching agent actually closes vulnerabilities, not vibes. How do we measure it?
A sensor box with 256MB RAM needs a small trainable classifier, and we can't ship Python.
We want our harness's planner and retry policies to improve week over week, with receipts an auditor could replay.
Route the easy 80% of tickets to a cheap model and escalate only the ones it demonstrably fails.
TypeScript shop, tired of prompt spaghetti — we want composable LLM programs with optimizers.
We need dozens of ready agent roles orchestrated in a mesh with cost tracking across model providers.
Bare-metal box, multiple tenants, strict isolation — we want hypervisor partitions, not containers.
Our ADRs say one thing and the code does another; we want decision records treated as living plans and checked against reality.
A thousand users each need their own agent memory, but full copies are killing our storage bill.
We'll only accept a self-optimizing system if every change is independently benchmarked, signed, and reversible.
Same agent program, three model vendors, one bill we can actually attribute per task.
